status_summary: On 2025-03-27 HHS announced a restructuring that would combine OASH with HRSA, SAMHSA, ATSDR and NIOSH into a new Administration for a Healthy America and consolidate redundant units; the release does not mention the Surgeon General or the Commissioned Corps. As of August 2025 Congress had not created or funded the new agency and a federal court had temporarily blocked parts of the reorganization, and a House Appropriations Committee bill advanced on 2026-06-09 again did not fund it. No step merging the Assistant Secretary for Health and Surgeon General posts or restructuring the Commissioned Corps was found.

title: Combine the Assistant Secretary for Health and Surgeon General into one four-star post
uncertainties: The HHS release was re-read in review: it lists OASH among the offices folded into the Administration for a Healthy America and describes consolidating 28 divisions into 15, but does not mention the Surgeon General or the Commissioned Corps; the source title is a descriptive label for a release titled HHS Announces Transformation to Make America Healthy Again. A news report of 2025-08-18 states Congress had not moved to create the new agency and that a federal judge in Rhode Island temporarily blocked HHS reorganization efforts; the court order was not read and is not a timeline event. A Surgeon General nomination made in May 2025 is an appointment to the existing post, not a merger. The House committee action comes from a stakeholder report and was not checked against committee documents. Court action and any Federal Register statement of organization for OASH were not located.
